ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before accepting any engagement, the firm must screen all proposed shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories, counterparties and client-funded litigation parties against: (1) OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists; (2) UN Security Council Consolidated Lists; (3) PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs restrictive lists; (4) Taiwan Ministry of Justice designated individuals and entities; (5) EU and UK sanctions lists; (6) PEP databases and adverse media. The screening must cover real-time global alerts, and any match triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and escalation to the AML compliance officer. Results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company and Commerce One-Stop Service Portal - Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be in Traditional Chinese characters; Simplified Chinese, pinyin romanization, or foreign scripts do not constitute a valid statutory name. The name must follow the four-tier naming doctrine: distinctive trade name plus business scope description plus legal form suffix. An English name may be filed for trade and customs purposes but it is not a substitute for the Chinese statutory name. All official filings with the MOEA central company registry must use Traditional Chinese, and any foreign-language documentation must be accompanied by a certified Traditional Chinese translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of receiving a written rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the Department of Commerce of the Ministry of Economic Affairs under the Taiwan Administrative Appeal Act, attaching the rejected application, the official rejection notice, amended alternative company names, and a legal memorandum distinguishing the cited conflicting names. If the rejection is due to a sensitive token requiring a license, the applicant must attach the competent authority's prior license, consent, or irrelevance certificate. The appeal must also explain how the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company or trade name in the same industry. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may initiate administrative litigation in the Taipei High Administrative Court within two months from service of the denial decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For ISIC 6910 commercial litigation chambers, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the principal statutory registered office. Taiwan company registration, bank account opening, and IOLTA trust account administration require a physical operating location where corporate books and client matter files are maintained. The National Taxation Bureau will reject a virtual-only arrangement for sales tax and profit-seeking enterprise registration, and most reputable banks in Taiwan will refuse to open a business or IOLTA trust account without verified physical occupancy, lease ownership, signage, and personnel. A virtual office may be used only as an auxiliary correspondence address, never as the registered office for a legal services entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk level: High - approximately 75% probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation. Checklist for inspection readiness: company signage at the registered address; lease or title document in the company's name; physical desks, filing cabinets, and IT infrastructure; original accounting books and client ledger records; IOLTA trust account statements matching client matter balances; employees physically present during business hours; tax invoices and payroll records on site; and business stationery demonstrating the registered address. Unannounced inspections are conducted by National Taxation Bureau, MOEA commercial administration officials, and labor insurance authorities. Virtual-office setups, low declared capital, insufficient employees, or mismatched tax registration will materially elevate the likelihood of sanctions, license suspension, and adverse findings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, Articles 1, 6, 8, 12, 101, 128, 129, 156, 172, 192, 203, 208 and 228; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 4, 7 and 8; Regulations Governing Permission for Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area Investors; Lawyers Act, Articles 5, 6 and 21; Foreign Lawyers Act, Articles 10 through 14.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs (MOEA DCA), Company Registration Division, Taiwan Company and Business E-Registration System
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application and Articles of Incorporation, the standard Taiwan registration form submitted under Article 6 of the Taiwan Company Act through the MOEA E-Registration System
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed on a limited company under the Taiwan Company Act; the government does not require an escrow account as a condition of company formation. Nevertheless, for entities using foreign investment, the remitted paid-in capital must pass through an escrowed bank account and be verified by a certified public accountant. For legal-services chambers, the Taiwan Bar Association imposes separate solvency and IOLTA trust accounting requirements, but no minimum capital deposit is fixed by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_JV_LTD, having been duly convened on this ____ day of ____, 20____, at the registered office in Taipei, Taiwan, with notice duly waived in writing by all directors and a quorum present throughout. The following resolutions are adopted and each shall take effect upon issuance of the Company Registration Certificate by the Ministry of Economic Affairs. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUANCE. RESOLVED, that the authorized share capital of the Company is fixed at ____ New Taiwan Dollars divided into ____ ordinary shares; that the paid-in share capital shall be subscribed and paid in cash to the escrow account of the Company at ____ Bank; that no share shall be deemed issued until full payment has been verified by the certified public accountant; and that any issuance of shares to a foreign or mainland-area investor is conditional upon the approval of the Investment Commission. 2. BANKING AND TRUST AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that ____ Bank is designated the principal banking institution; that the Managing Director and the Compliance Officer are authorized, jointly, to execute all banking and wire transfer instruments, and separately to operate the IOLTA client trust account; that client funds shall be held only in the IOLTA trust account, shall not be commingled with the operating funds, and shall be disbursed strictly in accordance with the Taiwan Bar Association trust accounting rules. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is established at ____, Taipei, Taiwan; that the Managing Director is directed to execute the lease, utility, and insurance contracts; and that business at that office is authorized only after the municipal business license and fire safety certification are obtained. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that ____ is elected Chairperson; ____ is appointed Managing Director; ____ is appointed Corporate Secretary; and ____ is appointed Compliance Officer and anti-money-laundering reporting officer. 5. DELEGATED AUTHORITY. RESOLVED, that the Managing Director, with the Compliance Officer, is specifically authorized to file the company registration, tax registration, law firm establishment application, IOLTA bank account documentation, AML policy manual, and all ancillary applications necessary for the lawful commencement of the cross-border commercial litigation practice. 6. GENERAL. RESOLVED, that certified copies of these resolutions be transmitted to the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Justice, Taipei City Government, the National Taxation Bureau, and the designated bank, and that any director or officer may sign all instruments necessary to effect the foregoing resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs (MOEA DCA) and Investment Commission (MOEAIC), Taiwan E-Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the company name reservation and the foreign investment approval request simultaneously through the MOEA E-Registration System. The Chinese parent entity must provide a notarized certificate of incorporation, a board resolution authorizing the investment, and a capital source declaration. If the parent is a mainland-area company, the Investment Commission will screen the proposed legal-services industry under the Mainland Area Investment Permission Regulations; commercial litigation may be restricted, so an advance ruling must be obtained. The online form must identify the exact ISIC 6910 scope, the proposed statutory officers, and the Chinese and English company names. Failing to provide complete beneficial-ownership identification or prior investment approval will result in a protocol suspension.
required_dossiers: notarized certificate of incorporation of the Chinese parent entity
board resolution authorizing outward investment
capital source and beneficial ownership declaration
foreign investment application form
Chinese and English company name reservation form
power of attorney to formation agent
advance ruling or permission letter for mainland-area investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is denied for similarity, the applicant must either obtain a written consent letter from the prior registrant or file an alternate name as a new reservation. If the investment application is suspended due to restricted industry classification, the shareholder must restructure the ownership vehicle, apply for a discretionary exception, or seek an administrative appeal before the Investment Commission within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Notarization and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA DCA; Taipei District Court Notary Office or licensed notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Traditional Chinese. The shareholders meeting shall approve the capitalization, transfer restrictions, election of directors, and the registered office. Thereafter, convene the first board meeting and adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution set out in this dossier. All foreign-issued certificates and powers of attorney must be notarized and legalized in the issuer jurisdiction and authenticated by the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office or apostille authority recognized by Taiwan. The executed Articles, shareholders meeting minutes, board resolutions, and legal representative identification are submitted to MOEA DCA online or in person. The MOEA checks the company name availability and documentary completeness; any insufficiency must be corrected within fifteen days.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation in Traditional Chinese
signed shareholders meeting minutes
First Board Resolution
share subscription agreement
certified copies of passports or corporate registration of all subscribers
notarized and legalized power of attorney
apostille or consular authentication certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the notarial chain, the formation agent shall re-notarize the defect document and file a supplemental legalization certificate. If the articles violate a mandatory provision, the board shall adopt an amending resolution and resubmit the revised articles without loss of priority if filed within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution, Foreign Exchange Verification and IOLTA Trust Ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Bank of China Foreign Exchange Department; licensed custodian bank in Taiwan; certified public accountant registered with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow bank account in the name of the company in formation at a Taiwan licensed bank, then receive paid-in capital by international wire. The foreign shareholder must file a foreign exchange remittance certificate with the Central Bank, and the receiving bank will issue a foreign currency remittance notice. The certified public accountant verifies the bank statement, subscription ledger, board resolution, and investment approval, then issues a capital verification report. For a legal-chambers entity, a segregated IOLTA trust ledger must be opened for client funds. The trust account may be opened after the law firm license is conditionally granted; the responsible attorney signs a common trust account declaration. All capital documents are lodged with the registration file before the MOEA issues the company registration.
required_dossiers: temporary escrow account certificate
Central Bank foreign exchange remittance report
foreign currency remittance notice from the bank
CPA capital verification report
bank subscription payment receipts
share allotment list
IOLTA trust account declaration signed by responsible attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Central Bank rejects the remittance report, the shareholder must re-document the source of funds and file a revised declaration. If the CPA refuses verification, the company must return the capital to the remitter, correct the subscription ledger, and re-credit the escrow account under the same investment approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration, Tax Registration and Municipal Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA DCA; National Taxation Bureau of Taipei (Ministry of Finance); Taipei City Government Department of Economic Development
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed company registration application through the MOEA E-Registration System, attaching the Articles of Incorporation, the First Board Resolution, the capital verification report, the foreign investment approval, and registered-office lease or title documentation. The MOEA will register the company and issue the Company Registration Certificate and the unified business number. Within fifteen days, apply to the National Taxation Bureau for income tax and Uniform Invoice registration, and to the Taipei City Government for the municipal business license. Register the company with the labor, health, and pension insurance system and with the local commercial register. If the MOEA issues a corrective notice, amend and resubmit within thirty days; the company may continue preparatory activities if it has not commenced revenue operations.
required_dossiers: MOEA company registration application form
Articles of Incorporation and First Board Resolution
CPA capital verification report
MOEAIC foreign investment approval
registered office lease or title deed
Taiwan tax and uniform invoice registration forms
director and legal representative identification documents
labor, health and pension insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires an additional use-classification permit, apply for a change-of-use certificate under the Taipei City Building Management Ordinance and file the certificate as a supplementary response to the corrective notice. If tax registration is queried, provide the company seal certificate and the signed authorization letter to the tax registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Law Firm Licensing, Fire Safety and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Legal Affairs Administration; Taiwan Taipei District Bar Association; Taipei City Fire Department; Ministry of Labor Occupational Safety and Health Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Since the venture is classified under ISIC 6910 as a cross-border commercial litigation chamber, the responsible Taiwan-licensed attorney must file a law firm establishment application with the Ministry of Justice, and the foreign attorney must obtain a foreign legal affairs lawyer permit under the Foreign Lawyers Act. Submit the Taipei City business license application, the fire safety certification application, and the occupational safety self-inspection. The Taipei City Fire Department will inspect the office premises for exit routes, fire extinguishers, and electrical safety. The Ministry of Labor inspectors will review the office risk assessment and employee emergency-response plan. Once all documents are approved, the board adopts the AML compliance manual, appoints the Compliance Officer, and files the financial intelligence unit registration. The package must be refiled if any license is suspended.
required_dossiers: law firm establishment application to the Ministry of Justice
attorney license of the responsible Taiwan-licensed attorney
foreign legal affairs lawyer permit application
Taipei City business license application
fire safety certification application and floor plan
occupational safety self-inspection checklist
AML compliance manual and FIU registration form
IOLTA account approval letter from the Bar Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Justice denies the law firm license due to incomplete attorney registration, the responsible attorney must first complete Taiwan Bar Association registration and resubmit. If fire safety inspection fails, remedy the marked deficiencies and request a re-inspection within thirty days. If the mainland-area investment is prohibited in legal services, the foreign ownership structure must be divested before any further license proceedings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Justice, Legal Affairs Administration; Taipei City Government Department of Economic Development
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Taiwan Law Firm Registration Certificate, Foreign Legal Affairs Attorney Permit, and Taipei City Business License for Legal Services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable; no physical manufacturing, chemical process, assembly plant, or warehousing facility is established under ISIC 6910. The office-only occupancy does not require an Environmental Impact Assessment or central environmental permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; no process wastewater, VOC stream, or hazardous waste is generated. Office waste handling must conform to the Waste Disposal Act, including licensed recycling contracts for toner and electronic equipment and general municipal waste collection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Required: fire safety certification from the Taipei City Fire Department under the Fire Services Act, a structural occupancy approval from the building authority, and an occupational safety and health clearance from the Ministry of Labor for the office premises. These certificates must be posted at the registered office, renewed biennially, and kept in the statutory company records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Tax Administration (National Taxation Bureaus in Taipei, Kaohsiung, and regional branches); online electronic portal: Ministry of Finance E-Tax Network (etax.nat.gov.tw) and the E-Invoice Cloud Platform (einvoice.nat.gov.tw)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Register the entity with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) through the Company Registration and Electronic Application Gateway; for foreign-invested structures obtain pre-approval from the MOEA Investment Commission under the Foreign Investment Act. 2. Upon approved company registration, the competent National Taxation Bureau automatically issues a Unified Business Number (UBIN), which concurrently serves as the VAT registration identifier and corporate income tax account number. 3. For foreign non-resident juridical persons with no Taiwan establishment but engaging in taxable cross-border digital services, file a Business Tax registration application with the National Taxation Bureau through a local tax representative, attaching the jurisdictional corporate certificate, board resolution appointing the tax representative, and a power of attorney. 4. Provide the registered local business address, principal activity descriptions, estimated monthly sales volume, and the responsible local person's identity details. 5. Receive the Unified Business Number certificate and, if applicable, an electronic tax-digital certificate for online filing. 6. Maintain the registration with the tax authority, updating within 15 days after any change in ownership, address, business scope, or responsible person.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch classification election mechanisms. Corporate entities are inherently subject to entity-level taxation under the Income Tax Act, and no pass-through treatment is available for limited companies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Business Tax (VAT) under the Business Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory full VAT registration is triggered when average monthly taxable sales exceed NT$200,000 for goods and services. Foreign e-commerce service providers supplying digital or downloadable services to individuals in Taiwan must register for VAT when annual turnover from Taiwan sources exceeds NT$480,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registered VAT taxpayers must issue serialized Uniform Invoices for all taxable sales. Electronic Uniform Invoices (Cloud Invoices) must be transmitted to the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Platform within 48 hours of issuance using the Turnkey network connection or application programming interface (API). There is no real-time fiscal diary stamping regime, but the 48-hour batch transmission rule, embedded inspection codes, and annual anti-fraud audit controls operate as the statutory fiscal clearance mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, a zero rate applies to exported goods that physically leave Taiwan customs territory, and to services rendered to foreign enterprises or overseas persons where the service is actually used or consumed outside Taiwan. Cross-border commercial litigation and legal advisory services qualify when the client is a foreign entity, the work is performed for use in foreign proceedings or foreign commercial arbitration, and the benefit of the service occurs outside Taiwan. Offshore digital legal services supplied to non-resident customers and paid for from foreign currencies also qualify if the customer's place of establishment and place of use are wholly outside Taiwan.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration System output certified by Taiwan Customs)
Bill of Lading or International Air Waybill evidencing physical shipment from Taiwan
Zero-rated Uniform Invoice clearly marked as exported supply
Foreign exchange remittance/settlement certificate issued by an authorized foreign exchange bank in Taiwan
Original client agreement, statement of work, and communication records evidencing that the legal service was rendered for external consumption outside Taiwan
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: National Taxation Bureau audit procedures require full preservation of all export/zero-rating documents for a minimum of five years. If zero-rating is found to be unsupported, fraudulent, or failing to meet the foreign use and consumption test, the tax authority will claw back the difference between zero-rated and 5% VAT, impose arrears interest, and apply administrative penalties under the Business Tax Act ranging from one to five times the underpaid tax. Deliberate misrepresentation or fictitious export documentation can lead to criminal prosecution for tax evasion, seizure of assets, and disqualification from future zero-rating or expedited refund treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC) is the sole regulator for foreign exchange and cross-border payments; PBOC is the monetary authority and central clearing overseer (CNAPS/CIPS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates full current-account convertibility for trade and service cross-border receipts/payments, while capital-account transactions remain subject to SAFE filing, approval, or designated-bank verification. For the Sino-foreign JV, lawful RMB profits and distributable dividends may be converted and remitted abroad after annual statutory audit, corporate income tax settlement and clearance, and confirmation through the capital account information system; no material convertibility hurdle exists beyond standard tax, SAFE, and bank validation of legitimate source and use.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SAFE Trade Foreign Exchange Name List system, there is no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts; the JV may retain export foreign exchange in a domestic designated FX settlement account. However, export proceeds must be repatriated to a licensed domestic bank within 180 days from the export declaration date under the prior verification regime, which remains the benchmark commercial expectation for timely receipt. All export proceeds are subject to total-amount trade verification and must be supported by customs declarations, invoices, contracts, and logistics documents; voluntary conversion to RMB is permitted at market rate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account / Pending-Settlement RMB Account / Operational Account
Capital Account and Litigation Disbursement Operating Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary settlement rail. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) are not permitted to open resident RMB settlement accounts or execute RMB FX settlements on behalf of the JV without a licensed onshore bank partner and SAFE filing. They may only provide ancillary foreign-currency collection support if backed by a domestic designated bank and compliant with PBOC payment licensing; otherwise legal and regulatory blockers include the unapproved cross-border FX settlement, AML data sovereignty, and CNAPS/CIPS clearing incompatibility.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical presence. The legal representative, board-designated manager, and financial controller must appear in person at the bank branch for a face-to-face AML/KYC interview; remote or fully digital account opening is not permissible for a newly incorporated Sino-foreign equity joint venture. The interview includes biometric verification, signature countersigning, source-of-wealth confirmation, and review of the entity's constitutional documents and licensed legal practice credentials.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Litigation proceeds or settlement payments received from foreign counterparties or pooled law-firm client accounts with an unclear transactional chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client engagement agreements, court or arbitral award excerpts, payment entitlement and fee-split breakdown, JV-issued invoice, notarised beneficial ownership certificate, client source-of-funds declaration countersigned by the responsible attorney, and a bank-specific transaction pedigree report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border disbursements to overseas co-counsel, legal experts, forensic accountants, and asset-tracing vendors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Service agreements with clear scope-of-work, outgoing invoice validation, beneficiary passport/registration proof, internal AML/KYC review sheet, record of withholding tax and VAT/service-tax clearance, and a compliance officer approval memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IOLTA/trust-account movement and pooled client balances trigger enhanced due diligence for a legal-sector entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trust deed or escrow agreement, client-by-client trust ledger reconciliation, monthly bank-side trust balance report, designated AML/compliance officer appointment letter, and prior-years audited financial statements demonstrating segregation of trust funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait and international sanctions exposure from litigation involving Taiwan, mainland China, or third-country sanctioned counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-approved OFAC/UN sanctions screening results, litigation privilege memo describing the legitimate legal mission, transaction counterparty pedigree analysis, sworn confirmation that all parties are not designated persons, and a prescribed post-transaction monitoring report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholders shall remit FDI equity injection by SWIFT MT103 using SAFE BOP transaction code for equity capital (FDI). Funds enter the JV's designated '外汇资本金账户' (FDI Capital Account) at a licensed domestic bank; the bank performs authenticity verification against the Foreign Investor Filing / FDI Certificate, capital contribution schedule, and business license registered scope. Each RMB settlement for operating expenses, litigation costs, payroll, and external counsel is recorded under SAFE's Foreign Exchange Settlement Declaration and reported through the '结汇待支付账户' mechanism; funds must not be applied to prohibited uses outside the registered business scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For professional legal-services settlements, foreign witness fees, and evidentiary procurement, the clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank instructions) routed via the domestic executing bank after invoice/contract valuation and proof of service delivery. Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700/MT707) and documentary collections are permissible only for supply-chain transactions relating to evidence databases, licensed legal research tools, court security instruments, and cross-border asset-tracing vendor procurement; all outbound disbursements require the enterprise to maintain valid Trade Foreign Exchange Name List status and provide a complete underlying transaction dossier.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB FX forwards (远期结售汇) for CNY/USD and CNY/EUR cash-flow hedging
Onshore FX options (外汇期权) including plain-vanilla and cost-reducing structured options
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts on CNY/TWD executed via licensed offshore NDF venues or designated bank bridges for cross-strait settlement exposure
Cross-currency swaps (货币掉期) between CNY and USD/TWD to finance long-tail litigation cost liabilities
FX swaps (外汇买卖/掉期) for temporary liquidity matching of litigation fee cycles, limited to trade or service-settlement underlying exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return and Settled Financial Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after fiscal year-end; 31 May for a calendar-year company, or the last day of May following the close of the accounting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 3% surcharge for the first two months and 6% for two to four months, capped at 10% of underpaid tax, plus daily overdue interest; continued non-filing permits the tax authority to assess income by estimation, impose tax liens, and pursue enforced collection; deliberate false reporting invokes criminal tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Business Report approved at the regular shareholders' meeting, evidenced by adopted minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records maintained for audit; evidence produced to the Ministry of Economic Affairs if the competent authority requires verification of governance compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Regular shareholders' meeting must be held within 6 months after fiscal year-end; by 30 June for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Where the regular shareholders' meeting is not convened by the statutory deadline, the competent authority may order convening and sanction responsible officers; continuing governance default can lead to a Ministry of Economic Affairs dissolution order, effectively deregistering the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Act Article 22-1 company and control-information declaration covering directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding more than 10% of the shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company Registration Repository, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the occurrence of each notifiable change; the annual register audit and beneficial-ownership synchronization should be completed by 31 December and re-verified before the 31 May tax filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the 15-day window, or filing inaccurate information, exposes the company to administrative fines up to NT$500,000 per violation; an inactive company that repeatedly defaults on compulsory registry notifications may be administratively deregistered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested operations report and audited financial statements of the joint venture, submitted in satisfaction of the foreign-investment approval conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; by 31 March for a calendar-year company, unless the investment approval letter prescribes a later but no less strict deadline no later than 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing may trigger Investment Commission corrective action, suspension of future investment applications and profit or capital remittances, and, in serious or repeated cases, revocation of foreign-investment approval leading to forced capital repatriation and winding-up.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified public accountant audit is mandatory under Company Act Article 20 where paid-in capital reaches NT$30 million or where the company meets the revenue threshold designated by the Ministry of Finance; a foreign-invested Sino-Foreign equity joint venture is also routinely required by the Investment Commission to submit audited Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards financial statements annually, even if the statutory size threshold is not met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards for statutory financial statements, aligned with IFRS; supplemented by the Business Entity Accounting Act and Regulations; income-tax-sensitive books and records are separately maintained under the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax settlement framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose a separate annual beneficial-owner filing for non-public companies; instead, control information must be declared under Company Act Article 22-1 within 15 days after each notifiable change. For the Sino-Foreign joint venture, the corporate secretary conducts an annual closing review by 31 December, obtains a written confirmation from each shareholder with direct or indirect ownership or control rights above 10%, verifies all share transfer proceedings, updates the share and UBO registers, and attaches the confirmation to the internal annual secretarial compliance certificate for production to the designated anti-money-laundering officer and auditors.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 to 1,500 per year for registered office and corporate secretarial services in Taiwan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to 8,000 per year for a compact listed-jurisdiction joint venture performing legal services; consolidated or group-audit support may add an additional USD 1,000 to 2,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for a Taiwan incorporated JV; eligible offshore dispute resolution services are not protected by special tax incentives. Preferential treatments available include R&D investment tax credits under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, deduction of professional liability insurance costs, and a 5% retained earnings surcharge on undistributed surplus. The scope of commercial litigation chambers is not categorized as a hi-tech pioneer enterprise; therefore, only ordinary cost deductions and transfer pricing compliance apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form 55) filed via the Taiwan Tax Portal (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw) or the integrated electronic filing network; equivalent paper form accepted in exceptional administrative circumstances.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due by the last day of the fifth month after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year enterprise the statutory deadline is May 31.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, Uniform Business Number, and registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan-incorporated JV is the resident taxpayer; non-resident shareholders do not file this return. The JV must enter the National Tax Bureau registration data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period of the tax return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the annual period YYYY/MM/DD to YYYY/MM/DD; foreign shareholders must align the dividend withholding calendar with this reported period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total business revenue (revenue from arbitration, commercial litigation, asset tracing, and related professional services).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue sourced from Taiwan cross-border commercial litigation is within the JV's worldwide taxable income; no non-resident allocation is permitted unless the JV can prove separate foreign PE accounting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs and expenses directly attributable to litigation: court filing fees, expert witness fees, external counsel charges, enforcement costs, and IOLTA trust administration expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Supporting contracts, invoices, and contemporaneous documentary evidence must be retained for tax inspection; non-resident parent allocations must satisfy arm's length TP rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income for the fiscal year after adjustments for transfer pricing, loss carryforward, and non-deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The JV must compute the tax base on a standalone enterprise basis; no automatic flow-through of losses or gains to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable after prepayments and DTA credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident JV settles the 20% CIT liability; subsequent distribution to the mainland Chinese parent triggers separate dividend withholding at source.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing after notice is punishable with a surcharge of 3% of the assessed tax amount; tax underpayment in arrears accrues at 1.5% per 30 days, capped at 15%, plus interest under the Tax Collection Act. Under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act, intentional false filing may result in a penalty of up to three times the evaded tax amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed to non-resident corporate shareholders, including mainland Chinese enterprises, unless reduced under an applicable cross-strait tax agreement protocol.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty or cross-strait agreement relief, the beneficial owner must submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), provide evidence of direct shareholding status, and file an application with the Tax Administration Bureau before the dividend settlement date. For mainland Chinese shareholders, the Cross-Strait Taxation Cooperation Agreement provides negotiated withholding rates; without an approved TRC and completed benefit claim, the statutory 21% rate is withheld. The payer must verify the recipient's beneficial ownership and maintain Form 6 withholding documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory WHT is 20% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Under the cross-strait tax agreement, interest may be reduced to 7% and royalties to 5% if the recipient is the beneficial owner and obtains a valid TRC; but excess withholding must be claimed through the administrative refund procedure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File and comprehensive transfer pricing report are mandatory when annual aggregate related-party transactions reach or exceed NT$200 million; a Master File is required for multinational groups with annual consolidated revenues above NT$30 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan has no codified general Economic Substance Regulation; however, tax authorities apply the substance-over-form rule, Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act, and OECD BEPS principles. A cross-border commercial litigation JV must maintain a real Taiwan office, qualified legal staff, an IOLTA trust account, board meeting records, case management protocols, and decision-making authority; otherwise tax benefits may be denied and the entity recharacterized as a tax conduit or shell entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting cross-border litigation fees, arbitration award receipts, or asset tracing commissions; creating fictitious subcontracted legal invoices; diverting client disbursements through private foreign bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of up to three times the evaded tax plus late surcharges; criminal liability under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act for fraud-based tax evasion, punishable by imprisonment up to five years and/or a fine of up to NT$60,000 in addition to restitution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or knowingly adopt false returns may have the corporate veil pierced for civil restitution; the National Tax Administration may impose travel bans, freeze personal bank accounts, and refer the case to the prosecutor for incarceration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Taiwan JV with no physical office, no professional staff payroll, no local client intake, and no substantive management of commercial litigation; directing arbitration and asset-tracing decisions from mainland China without local business function.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of revenue, disallowance of treaty or cross-strait tax benefits, retroactive transfer pricing adjustment, imposition of the 5% retained earnings surcharge on undistributed earnings, and possible forced deregistration of the JV.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for the underpaid tax and penalties when the tax authority concludes that the entity was used as an artificial arrangement; outstanding tax liabilities may trigger travel bans and civil execution against personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering Violation for Litigation Chambers
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to adopt Customer Due Diligence for high-net-worth commercial clients; accepting payment in cash above the statutory threshold without declaration; using the IOLTA trust account to mix client funds with operating fees or to obscure the destination of arbitration settlement funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines from NT$500,000 to NT$5 million for compliance failures under the Money Laundering Control Act; willful facilitation of money laundering may subject the firm to imprisonment up to seven years and corporate fines up to NT$50 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director and compliance officer are personally liable under the AML regime, with asset freezes, travel bans, and judicial seizure of individual bank accounts; company directors may be deported or detained when the cross-border settlement involves sanctioned counterparties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, management fees, or deemed dividends to the mainland Chinese parent without performing the 21% withholding; mislabeling dividends as loans, service fees, or IP royalties to avoid withholding; failing to submit the TRC supporting a reduced cross-strait rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may levy a penalty equal to 20% of the under-withheld tax, or up to three times for intentional evasion; unpaid withholding tax is recovered from the JV together with interest at the postal savings annual rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives are deemed statutory withholding agents; the unpaid WHT, penalties, and interest can be collected from directors' personal assets, and a director who knowingly authorized a disguised dividend distribution may face criminal restraint and imprisonment.
